species.real: Rheas have three toes on each foot and run in zigzags, sticking out one wing like a rudder to steer.
species.name: Choiquet

dex.text: A long-legged chick that zigzags across the steppe at a speed its legs did not warn you about.
dex.fact: Darwin's rhea, called choique in Patagonia, is a big flightless bird that can run at over 50 kilometres an hour, swerving to throw off a chase.

species.real: Darwin's party ate one of these rheas before he realised it was a new species, and he had to rescue the head, legs and wings from the leftovers.
species.name: Choique

dex.text: Runs the steppe as if it owns it, which, frankly, it did first. The father raises the chicks and will chase you off for looking.
dex.fact: In rheas the male builds the nest, sits on eggs laid by several females and raises the chicks alone. The smaller Patagonian species is named after Charles Darwin, who collected it on the Beagle voyage in the 1830s, after the crew had eaten most of one.
